content:
As WhatsApp gears up to officially roll out its username feature, the messaging app now allows users to save usernames along with names and phone numbers when storing contacts. Here's everything you need to know.

The username field when adding new contacts has now started rolling out to some WhatsApp users

While this is a common feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently started moving away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

Earlier this year, WhatsApp began rolling out a username reservation system, giving users the opportunity to secure their preferred handle ahead of the official username feature launch, in a bid to prevent impersonation by scammers.

Then, just weeks ago, the platform began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is starting to incorporate a username field when users add new contacts. The username field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo points out that the username field appears to be rolling out simultaneously to some users on both the WhatsApp beta and stable versions.

When testing with the latest stable version, although the username field has appeared, the system still displays a "this username is not on WhatsApp" message even when the username in question does exist.

That said, this marks WhatsApp finally catching up to its competitors and adding a feature that many consider a long-overdue basic.
